concept.name: Tick value
concept.definition: The monetary profit or loss on one contract resulting from a one-tick (minimum price fluctuation) move in the contract's price.
concept.intuition: Tick size tells you the smallest price step; tick value tells you how many dollars that step is worth in your account.
concept.mechanics: Tick value = tick size x contract size (for unit-quoted contracts) or tick size x contract multiplier (for point-quoted contracts). It is the atomic unit of P&L: total P&L = number of ticks moved x tick value x number of contracts.
concept.formula: Tick value = tick size x contract size (e.g., $0.01/barrel x 1,000 barrels = $10 per contract for WTI crude oil futures).
concept.failure_modes: Assuming a single tick value across contract variants (standard vs micro) or across currencies misstates risk; for contracts quoted in foreign currencies the tick value also varies with the FX rate.
concept.misconceptions: Traders sometimes quote risk in ticks without converting to dollars, which hides that identical tick counts imply very different dollar risks across products.
concept.example: With WTI crude futures at a tick size of $0.01 per barrel and a contract size of 1,000 barrels, a 12-tick favorable move on one contract earns 12 x $10 = $120.
